primitives.name: Slow Developers
primitives.verbatim_quote: 20 WINNING FOOTBALL presents himself at the field-house, but in putting a special and careful effort on the candidates who show little immediate promise.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Effort': 'Dimensionless coaching allocation', 'Impmediate Promise': 'Dimensionless measure of initial performance'}
primitives.assumptions: Coaches tend to allocate less effort to candidates showing immediate promise, creating a bias against slower-developing talent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When coaches fail to identify and support early-stage potential, leading to loss of foundational skills before they can mature.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Models the probability of long-term development given early-stage coaching investment. GSE - Represents the state-transition cost of neglecting foundational skill-building in favor of immediate performance.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking the proportion of players who improve significantly after receiving additional early-season coaching versus those who do not.

primitives.name: Relative Development
primitives.verbatim_quote: Some of the best players ever developed were drawn from this class of candidates—men who had failed to make prep-school teams because of relatively slow development, and who as freshmen or sophomores were still well behind their mates in football knowledge and experience.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(Elite Player)': 'Probability of becoming an elite player', 'P(Slow Development | Early Struggle)': 'Conditional probability of slow development given early academic/athletic struggle'}
primitives.assumptions: Initial academic or athletic underperformance does not preclude future elite achievement; relative timing matters more than absolute starting point.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure to account for individual developmental trajectories leads to premature exclusion of high-potential individuals.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Adjusts prior distributions for player performance based on delayed onset of peak capability. GSE - Captures the strategic value of investing in players whose current state lags behind peers but shows signs of converging.
layer2.telemetry: Comparing career trajectory metrics (e.g., peak performance age) between players initially rated low versus high by coaches.

primitives.name: Distraction Elimination
primitives.verbatim_quote: Such men are sometimes slow to take hold on the field and the first impulse of a coach overwhelmed with the distractions of trying to distinguish between a hun dred strange faces, is to clarify his problem by eliminating them at once.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Elimination Rate': 'Rate of player removal per observation session', 'Cognitive Load of Observation': 'Dimensionless measure of information processing strain on coach'}
primitives.assumptions: Coaches facing information overload will disproportionately remove players who require longer observation periods to assess accurately.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High cognitive load causes coaches to rely on heuristics rather than thorough evaluation, resulting in misclassification of potential.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Quantifies the trade-off between false positive elimination and false negative retention under observational constraints. GSE - Models the transition from exploratory to exploitative phases where distraction-driven pruning occurs.
layer2.telemetry: Measuring the correlation between the number of new recruits evaluated and the rate of dismissals made within the first week.
